title: Justice delayed or justice denied? Apple executive Vivek Tiwari case
content: In a case dating back to 2018, police constable Prashant Kumar Chaudhary was sentenced to 10 years for culpable homicide. He shot Apple executive Vivek Tiwari during a police encounter that led to Tiwari's death. The court acquitted co-accused constable Sandeep Kumar due to insufficient evidence against him. Tiwari’s family expressed dissatisfaction and plans to appeal both the sentence and acquittal.

title: Indian oil refiners are now sending ships into Hormuz to get cheaper oil - here's why
content: Indian oil refiners are now chartering tankers to travel through the Strait of Hormuz and collect crude from inside the Persian Gulf. This marks a notable change in their approach as they seek to lower costs and strengthen the reliability of their supply chains.

title: Bill Gates does not agree with possibility of AI Kill Switch
content: Bill Gates questions the reliability of AI Kill Switches in today's technology landscape. He points out that diligent monitoring and solid regulations are crucial to prevent exploitation by malicious actors. Emphasizing that AI technology remains under human oversight, Gates alerts to the risks of rogue individuals harnessing AI for destructive ends. To protect society, effective legislation that allows for AI growth while ensuring safety is of utmost importance.

title: Pentagon’s new war machine: Drone command, AI push and a plan for future battlefields
content: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has announced a restructuring of the Pentagon aimed at enhancing drone warfare capabilities. A new combatant command dedicated to autonomous warfare will be established to lead technological advancements. Hegseth introduced Project Agincourt to streamline military procurement and engage with private entrepreneurs in warfighting innovations. Additionally, Project Meridian will focus on future military domains and technologies essential for US dominance.

title: India crush Sri Lanka by 124 runs, set up Asian Games gold-medal clash vs Pakistan
content: India delivered a phenomenal performance in the Asian Games semifinal against Sri Lanka, setting a challenging target of 170 runs. Sri Lanka struggled dramatically, getting bowled out for a mere 45 runs, thanks to Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel's exceptional bowling. Ishan Kishan's impressive innings of 80 not out underpinned the team's success. India are now geared up to compete against Pakistan for the coveted gold medal.

title: Australian scientists used wheat scent to confuse mice, cutting seed loss by 74%
content: Australian scientists tested a non-toxic way to protect wheat seeds from mice by spraying diluted wheat germ oil across farm plots. The treatment camouflaged the smell mice use to locate seeds underground. In a 2021 field experiment in New South Wales, seed loss fell by 63 per cent during and after sowing, and by up to 74 per cent when plots were treated before planting.

title: Nuns painted over risqué Rome frescoes; restorers reveal them 300 years later
content: In a remarkable reveal, Villa Silvestri Rivaldi in Rome is showcasing its breathtaking Renaissance frescoes after three centuries of concealment. These enchanting artworks depict various mythological scenes and figures, unveiled through advanced restoration techniques like laser cleaning. Notable personalities such as Eurialo Silvestri and Pope Leo XI have connections to this charming villa, with the restoration project set to enhance public appreciation of its rich historical legacy.

title: World’s richest woman Alice Walton builds a $250 million tuition-free medical school
content: Alice Walton’s fortune remains closely tied to her family’s Walmart holdings, while her public work has increasingly focused on art, medicine and philanthropy. Forbes estimated her wealth at nearly $120 billion in March 2026. Outside Walmart, she has committed $250 million to a medical school and $350 million toward a new healthcare campus in Bentonville.

title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
content: In September, India's manufacturing sector experienced significant progress with rising demand and production levels. The HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index climbed to 55.1, reflecting vibrant business activity. Companies increased their hiring practices at the quickest rate since May, projecting a more positive outlook. Growth in new orders resulted in higher inventories, suggesting expectations of sustained demand, while input costs and selling prices also increased, with inflation remaining historically moderate.

title: Hero bike battery changed 3 times, still faces issues; court orders Rs 25,000
content: Nethi Radha Krishna faced numerous issues with his Hero Glamour BS6 motorcycle after purchasing it in September 2021. He reported various engine and electrical problems that persisted despite over seven service visits to the dealer. The district consumer commission found the service provided inadequate but did not prove an inherent defect in the motorcycle. They ordered the dealer to inspect, repair, and compensatory payments for the customer's inconvenience.

title: Bhubaneswar horror: Masked intruder enters home, rapes woman at gunpoint
content: A woman in Bhubaneswar reported a rape incident that occurred late on Wednesday night. She alleged that a masked intruder entered her home and assaulted her at gunpoint. The local police have filed a case and started an investigation into the incident. A suspect has been detained for questioning, and vital clues have been identified. Efforts are underway to review CCTV footage and trace the accused.

title: ‘Wanted to take over temple’: 2 priests killed, bodies set ablaze in UP village
content: Two elderly priests residing in a temple in Shahjahanpur district were recently murdered by a man. The accused, Sumit Singh, allegedly attacked them with a heavy object before igniting their bodies. Singh reportedly intended to seize control of the temple management following his release from jail. Both priests had long been caretakers of the shrine which had a land registered in one priest's name.

title: Gold price prediction: Where are gold and silver headed today?
content: Gold and silver price prediction today: MCX Gold has moved higher after taking support near the 147,000 levels, indicating renewed buying interest at lower levels. The price structure remains positive as gold continues to hold above its key support zone, suggesting that the broader uptrend is still intact.

title: Asian Games: Ganesh wins bronze as India finish with four compound archery medals
content: At the Asian Games 2026, Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru clinched a bronze medal in the men's individual compound archery event, triumphing over Vietnam's Cong Duc Dang with a score of 149 to 144. His exceptional accuracy is evident as 14 of his 15 arrows hit the 10s. This achievement marks India's fourth medal in compound archery, contributing to an overall tally of 63.

title: Scotch whisky gets cheaper in India after trade deal with US; check new prices
content: Under the India-UK agreement, the import tariff on British whisky was reduced to 75% from 150%, effectively cutting the rate by half. The tariff is scheduled to decline further to 40% over the next 10 years. However, the reduction in import duty does not result in a similar reduction in the final retail price.

title: Neerja in 1986, Machchhar in 2026: 2 heroes who put passengers before themselves
content: Neerja Bhanot, a flight attendant, showed immense courage during the 1986 hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 in Karachi. She helped many passengers escape despite the danger, ultimately sacrificing her life. In 2026, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot during a flight and successfully regained control of the aircraft. His actions prevented a mid-air disaster, saving 174 lives onboard.

title: Drive wrong, pay more: Karnataka mulls Rs 5,000 fine for repeat traffic offenders
content: The Karnataka government is considering increasing fines for traffic violations, particularly for habitual offenders. This proposal includes escalating penalties and accumulating negative points for repeat violations. Additionally, the government plans to ban half-helmets to enhance safety for two-wheeler riders. Measures for regulating low-speed electric two-wheelers and promoting carpooling are also under discussion. Efforts are being made to improve public transport facilities and enforce traffic rules more strictly.

title: Piyush Goyal gets a ‘trade minister for life’ tag from US trade chief at G20
content: At the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee, US trade representative Jamieson Greer discussed key trade issues with Indian minister Piyush Goyal. They focused on food security, steel overcapacity, and the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, which Greer suggested re-examining. Goyal emphasized the importance of distinguishing between legitimate measures and the weaponization of food supply chains. Discussions also included efforts toward finalizing an interim India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, enhancing cooperation in manufacturing.

title: Senior citizen wrongly paid tax on Rs 25.42L interest; ITAT orders Rs 9.91L refund
content: Each year, the senior citizen reported the interest earned from his investments in tax-free bonds under the ‘exempt income’ category in his income tax return (ITR). But made a mistake in one year. The man realised the error only after the deadline for filing a revised ITR had passed. He therefore approached the jurisdictional assessing officer (JAO) and filed a rectification application.

title: Asian Games: Manu, Prince win sailing silver as India’s medal tally reaches 62
content: Manu Francis and Prince Noble secured a silver medal in men’s skiff sailing at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Their final race concluded with a second-place finish, accumulating a total of 23 net points. The Indian duo's consistent performance included three second-place finishes and one race victory across the event. India’s overall medal tally for the Games rose to 62, showcasing their achievements in various sports.

title: Man in WagonR with ‘POLICE’ sticker caught stealing plant from Delhi-Dehradun E-way

The incident occurred on the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, although no complaints have been reported yet. Police are in the process of verifying the authenticity of the viral footage for further investigation. This incident follows a previous theft involving nearly 7,000 potted plants after a horticulture event.

They highlighted the suspension of several laws under the Representation of People Act and related rules. title: 5 money changes in Oct: Bulk FD rates, UPI MDR, SBI ATM limit cut, LPG KYC & more

title: Asian Games: India win women’s team squash bronze after Anahat Singh’s heartbreak
content: India's women's squash team claimed a bronze medal after facing a 1-2 defeat from Hong Kong in the semifinals. Anahat Singh's match was intense, yet she fell short despite holding match points. Tanvi Khanna fought back to equalise, but ultimately, Joshna Chinappa couldn't secure victory against Ho Tze Lok in the decisive match. This result contributes to India's notable achievement of four squash medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.

title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier

From October 1, 2026, users will need biometric Aadhaar authentication to book subsidized LPG refills. Failure to register will still allow access to LPG at market rates without any subsidies.

title: Captain Machchhar: The Mumbai pilot who emerged as the hero of flydubai flight
content: captain, who is learnt to be in mid 30s, managed to fight off the assailant and regain control of the aircraft despite being severely injured . he managed to save the plane from plunging - something the Boeing 737 MAX was very close to at that point of time .

title: SC refuses to unfreeze TMC bank accounts, asks Calcutta HC to expedite hearing
content: the Supreme Court dismissed a plea by the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction seeking permission to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts . a bench of justices noted that the election Commission has frozen the party symbol and that the larger question of who is entitled to the funds in the accounts remains pending adjudication . the court declined to interfere with a Calcutta High Court order that had rejected the request .

content: the pilot of a flydubai flight survived an apparent hijacking attempt a day ago . title: Rainfall 4th lowest since 2001: Monsoon deficit at 13%, officially a drought year
content: south Peninsular India receives 30% of its annual rainfall during northeast monsoon season . TN, Puducherry and Karaikal receive 48% of their annual rainfall . this is the fourth lowest seasonal rainfall since 2001 .

title: Will Warring resign as Punjab Congress president? His response: 'no comments'
